title: 23 Parties Will Meet Today. The DMK Won't Be There. The INDIA Bloc Has Never Looked This Fragile.
excerpt: Kejriwal met Mamata the night before a meeting his party won't attend. The DMK wants its seats moved away from Congress. And the alliance's first gathering since its worst election losses is about survival, not strategy.
body:
The INDIA opposition bloc will meet at the Constitution Club in New Delhi today in what is shaping up to be its most contentious gathering since the alliance was formed in 2023. Twenty-three parties have confirmed attendance. Two of the alliance's most powerful regional anchors — the DMK and AAP — will not be in the room.

Congress general secretary Jairam Ramesh confirmed the headcount on Sunday, posting on X: "23 political parties have confirmed participation in the INDIA janbandhan meeting at Constitution Club, New Delhi on Monday June 8, 2026, at 12 noon." He added: "Like India, the INDIA janbandhan continues to stand united through its diversity."

The diversity, at this point, is doing most of the heavy lifting.

## Mamata Shows Up. So Does Kejriwal — Separately.

Trinamool Congress chief Mamata Banerjee arrived in Delhi on Sunday, fresh off a devastating loss in the West Bengal assembly elections where the BJP swept her off her home turf. Her party is in internal turmoil — 58 MLAs have rallied behind expelled leader Ritabrata Banerjee in an open revolt against her leadership.

In a move that drew immediate attention, AAP convenor Arvind Kejriwal met Mamata at the Delhi residence of TMC MP Abhishek Banerjee on Sunday evening. The TMC described the interaction as "warm" and said the two leaders held "an extensive discussion on the road ahead."

The subtext is loaded. AAP formally left the INDIA alliance months ago and is not expected to attend Monday's meeting. Yet Kejriwal felt it necessary to meet Mamata the night before the gathering. The TMC issued a statement invoking 2029: "When the people of India unite, no force on earth can stop their march towards justice, dignity and a better future in 2029."

Whether that unity extends beyond a single evening at Abhishek Banerjee's house is the question nobody can answer yet.

## The DMK Boycott

The most consequential absence is the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam. With 22 MPs in the Lok Sabha, the DMK is one of the INDIA bloc's largest constituents. It is staying away because of what it calls Congress's "betrayal" in Tamil Nadu.

The rupture traces back to the 2026 Tamil Nadu assembly elections, where Congress unilaterally ended its alliance with the DMK after the post-election formation of a TVK-led government. The DMK has not forgiven the move. Party MP Kanimozhi has written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla seeking a change in seating arrangement so DMK members no longer sit alongside Congress in the House — a symbolic but pointed gesture.

The CPI(M) will attend, but not without reservations. State secretary Srinivas Rao said, "The Congress is not acting as a serious opposition. The INDIA bloc will be united only if Congress proves its charges against CPI."

## What Is Actually on the Agenda

The formal agenda has not been released, but the meeting is expected to address three things: a joint strategy ahead of the Rajya Sabha elections and upcoming byelections in several states, a coordinated opposition stance on what Ramesh called the Modi government's "snatching away the right to vote for millions of Indians," and a review of the post-election political landscape after the TMC's collapse in Bengal, Congress's gains in Kerala, and the BJP's consolidation across the Hindi belt.

Leaders expected at the table include Mamata Banerjee, Abhishek Banerjee, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Samajwadi Party president Akhilesh Yadav, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Uddhav Thackeray (likely joining virtually), RJD's Tejashwi Yadav, PDP's Mehbooba Mufti, and representatives from the National Conference, NCP (Sharad Pawar faction), CPI, CPI(ML), VCK, IUML, and over a dozen smaller parties.

## The Diaspora Is Watching

For NRIs tracking Indian politics, the INDIA bloc's internal dynamics are a barometer of whether 2029 will produce a credible opposition challenge or another BJP walkover. The alliance's ability to hold together despite state-level fractures — Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Delhi — will determine whether it can offer a coherent alternative to the Modi government's third term.

The meeting begins at noon. The real test is what comes after it.
